_comment: Master catalog of BUMP-confirmed behavioural breaks selected for this study. Each entry is anchored to a real BUMP TEST_FAILURE reproduction (breaking_commit -> data/benchmark_test_failures/<sha>.json + reproductionLogs/successfulReproductionLogs/<sha>.log). The failing test + exception are recorded inline in each entry's characterization block; the `characterize` stage that extracted them from BUMP logs was removed on 2026-08-13 with mine/bbc_pipeline.py, since reproductionLogs/ no longer exists. SHAs verified against data/benchmark_test_failures on 2026-07-06.
_provenance: MIXED SOURCES. Most entries are curated from BUMP (chains-project/breaking-updates), failureCategory=TEST_FAILURE, javaVersionUsedForReproduction=11 — these have a populated 'clients' array with breaking_commit(s). A GROWING MINORITY are EXTERNAL breaks mined from security advisories (OSV Maven feed via mine_advisories.py), NOT from BUMP: these carry a top-level "provenance":"EXTERNAL_ADVISORY_NOT_BUMP" flag plus an 'external_source' block, have an empty 'clients' array (no BUMP breaking_commit), and are found via 'mine-commits'+'classify' rather than 'characterize'/'run'.

breaks.why_it_breaks: commons-io 2.8.0 added strict input validation (FileUtils.requireFile). FileUtils.copyFile(srcFile, destFile) with a DIRECTORY as srcFile now throws an UNCHECKED java.lang.IllegalArgumentException ('Parameter 'srcFile' is not a file: <path>'), where <=2.7 threw a CHECKED IOException. Client code with catch(IOException) around copyFile no longer catches it, so the failure escapes to the production path.

characterization.signal: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Parameter 'srcFile' is not a file: <path> at org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils.requireFile / FileUtils.copyFile. commons-io 2.8+ throws unchecked IAE where 2.7 threw checked IOException.

brief.what_changed: logback 1.4.0 moves to the SLF4J 2.x ServiceLoader binding and drops org.slf4j.impl.StaticLoggerBinder. A client still pinned to slf4j-api 1.7.x binds nothing: LoggerFactory silently falls back to a NOP logger, so logging output disappears rather than erroring. Where the old binder class is referenced directly, or a 1.7-era appender/config API is used, it fails harder.

Adaptations typically switch to wholeText(), set outputSettings().prettyPrint(false) or indentAmount/maxPaddingWidth, or update expected strings.

breaks.why_it_breaks: Security framework changed to default-deny at 1.4.18: unregistered classes now rejected on deserialization (ForbiddenClassException).

verify.signal_grep: ForbiddenClassException|NoTypePermission|security framework of XStream not initialized|no security framework configured

brief.what_changed: XStream changed its security model from a blacklist (deny a few known-dangerous types, allow everything else) to a whitelist (allow only a small set of built-in types, deny everything else). Client code that unmarshals its own domain types without first calling allowTypes / allowTypesByWildcard / addPermission still compiles and still marshals correctly, but now throws at unmarshal time. Marshalling (object -> XML) is unaffected; the break is on the read path.
brief.expected_signal_hint: com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException (wrapped in a ConversionException / CannotResolveClassException) raised from fromXML/unmarshal on a client domain type
brief.signal_pattern: ForbiddenClassException|NoTypePermission|security framework of XStream not initialized|no security framework configured

Until now it was mined on the adaptation axis only, which found 50 rows and 0 production adaptations -- the same result xstream gave before the bump axis took it from 20 candidates to 11 confirmed crossings. Its signal_quality is 'weak' precisely because the adaptation is config-shaped (setMaxDepth / input restructuring) and has no distinctive exception-handling idiom to search for; the bump axis does not depend on the adaptation having a searchable signature, which is why it is the right tool here. CVE-2023-1370 is the driver, so 'CVE' and 'security update' are live terms.

breaks.why_it_breaks: org.json tightened type coercion: JSONObject.getString() (and similar) on a non-string value (e.g. an Integer) now throws org.json.JSONException ('... is not a string') instead of coercing. Compiles fine; throws at runtime -> semantic break. Adaptation: use a coercing accessor (optString / String.valueOf(get(...))).

characterization.signal: org.json.JSONException: JSONObject["id"] is not a string (class java.lang.Integer : 0).

verify.note: Boundary pinned EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-04 by running JSONObject("{\"id\":0}").getString("id") against real jars: 20090211 COERCES (returns "0"); 20131018 and every later release THROW. The boundary is 20131018, not the catalogued to_version 20230227. Only the exception WORDING changed after that: '... not a string.' (<=20190722) -> '... is not a string' (20200518+) -> '... is not a string (class java.lang.Integer : 0)' (20220924+). Previously this field read 'the release that added strict getString coercion', which has no digits, so _parse_ver returned None and _crosses_boundary was False for EVERY candidate — traversal could never confirm anything for this break, silently.

breaks.why_it_breaks: H2 2.0 was a major SQL-compatibility overhaul (new reserved keywords, stricter typing/casting, changed defaults). Queries/schema that worked on 1.x now fail at runtime (surfaces here as org.hibernate...SqlException). Compiles fine -> semantic break. Adaptation: MODE=LEGACY or NON_KEYWORDS=... in the JDBC URL, or rename reserved-word columns.

breaks.why_it_breaks: snakeyaml 2.0 (CVE-2022-1471) makes SafeConstructor the effective default via a restrictive LoaderOptions TagInspector: new Yaml().load(...) no longer instantiates arbitrary Java types from YAML global tags. YAML that maps to application types (custom '!!com.example.Foo' tags) that 1.x deserialized now throws at load time. Client code still compiles; it throws at runtime on previously-accepted input -> semantic break. Adaptation: pass an explicit Constructor, or configure LoaderOptions.setTagInspector(tag -> tag.getClassName().equals(...)) / a trusted-tag inspector to re-allow the needed types.

characterization.signal: org.yaml.snakeyaml.constructor.ConstructorException / YAMLException: 'Global tag is not allowed' (or 'could not determine a constructor for the tag') — 2.0 restrictive TagInspector rejects arbitrary-type YAML that 1.x accepted.
characterization.note: Characterization derived from the advisory + the known 2.0 API change, NOT a BUMP repro log. Confirm the exact exception message at verify time.

trigger.description: A GLOBAL tag naming a Java class (e.g. !!com.example.Foo). snakeyaml 2.0's default TagInspector rejects exactly these. Requiring a dot excludes the standard YAML tags (!!str, !!int, !!map), which are never rejected. LOCAL tags (single !, resolved from the constructor's own yamlConstructors map) also do NOT reach the inspector, so they must not match.
trigger.note: A client whose YAML contains no global tag cannot experience this break, however cleanly it compiles and however real its bump. Verified on adityajoy-1902/Dashboard-V-2: root-type Constructor(Application.class) with tag-free YAML -> the adaptation was purely a compile migration.
trigger.unknown_if: YAML is supplied at runtime rather than bundled in the repo; then the trigger is undecidable from source.

verify.note: VERIFIED — see verify_status (3-state differential green 2026-07-20). Clean default-deny (direct xstream analogue). Adaptation = explicit Constructor / LoaderOptions.setTagInspector. First EXTERNAL-mined break fed through the pipeline.

assessment.reason: snakeyaml 2.0 removed EVERY constructor overload that does not take a LoaderOptions. Measured with javap: Constructor at 1.32 offers (), (LoaderOptions), (Class), (Class, LoaderOptions), (TypeDescription); at 2.0 ONLY the LoaderOptions-bearing variants survive. SafeConstructor at 1.32 offers () and (LoaderOptions); at 2.0 only (LoaderOptions). So any client that explicitly constructs a Constructor or SafeConstructor — the common 1.x idiom — fails at javac when it crosses to 2.x and NEVER REACHES the runtime tag-inspection change. The behavioural break is real but is shadowed by a syntactic one on the same classes.

breaks.why_it_breaks: jackson 2.10 locked down polymorphic default typing (CVE series). enableDefaultTyping() was deprecated in favour of activateDefaultTyping(PolymorphicTypeValidator); polymorphic deserialization of types not permitted by the validator throws com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidDefinitionException / InvalidTypeIdException at runtime. Adaptation: supply a BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator allowlist. TO BE CONFIRMED from real diffs — jackson default-typing has an API-migration confound (enableDefaultTyping deprecated 2.10, removed 2.12), so verify the actual break shape before designing the differential.

breaks._provenance_note: NOT from BUMP and NOT from the CVE advisory feed. This is external-mining discovery SOURCE #2 (library changelog / release notes): jackson-core 2.15.0 added StreamReadConstraints default parser limits. A genuine 'same code, new version, now throws' behavioural break (the clean jackson break, unlike the REJECTED default-typing one). No BUMP breaking_commit; clients found via mine-commits.
breaks.why_it_breaks: jackson-core 2.15.0 introduced StreamReadConstraints with default parser limits: maxNestingDepth=1000, maxNumberLength=1000, maxNameLength, maxStringLength (5M in 2.15.0, 20M in 2.15.1+). JSON exceeding a limit that 2.14 parsed fine now throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException at parse time. Code compiles unchanged; it throws at runtime on previously-accepted input -> behavioural break. Adaptation: build a JsonFactory with relaxed StreamReadConstraints, e.g. JsonFactory.builder().streamReadConstraints(StreamReadConstraints.builder().maxNestingDepth(N).maxStringLength(N).build()).build().

characterization.signal: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.exc.StreamConstraintsException: 'Document nesting depth (1001) exceeds the maximum allowed (1000...)' / 'String value length ... exceeds the maximum allowed' / 'Number value length ... exceeds the maximum allowed'.

verify.note: Clean same-code-now-throws limit break (json-smart max-depth analogue). Parent uses plain new ObjectMapper() (stable across 2.14/2.15); adapted uses the 2.15-only StreamReadConstraints API (separate compile profile).

breaks.why_it_breaks: 1.2.83 (CVE-2022-25845) tightens autoType: deserializing a JSON document carrying an @type tag into an arbitrary class is refused unless the type is explicitly permitted. Client code still COMPILES -- no signature changed, confirmed by a javap API diff showing 0 removals -- and throws at runtime on documents 1.2.80 accepted. The adaptation is an explicit re-permit: ParserConfig.getGlobalInstance().addAccept("com.foo."), setAutoTypeSupport(true), or safeMode configuration. Structurally the same shape as xstream allowTypes, which is the only shape that has yielded verified cases.

Passes every structural filter: boundary 2019-07 (old enough that clients have genuinely crossed, unlike the 2026 Camel entries), ZERO public API removed 1.9.3 -> 1.9.4 per javap diff (no compile break to shadow the behaviour, unlike snakeyaml), and it is ordinary infrastructure coded against directly by thousands of applications (unlike json-smart, which is transitive, and unlike fastjson, whose corpus is dominated by exploit demos).
breaks.why_it_breaks: 1.9.4 (CVE-2019-10086) registers SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_CLASS by DEFAULT, so the bean property named "class" is no longer introspectable. BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-09 by running PropertyUtils.getProperty(bean, "class") against both jars on JDK 11: 1.9.3 returns the Class object; 1.9.4 throws NoSuchMethodException ("Unknown property class on class ..."). The class SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector exists in BOTH jars -- only the default registration changed -- so client code COMPILES unchanged and fails at run time. Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit, structurally the same as xstream allowTypes: PropertyUtils.getPropertyUtils().removeBeanIntrospector(SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_CLASS).

breaks._provenance_note: From the OSV Maven feed (GHSA-cgp8-4m63-fhh5 / CVE-2021-37533), selected 2026-08-10 from the VALIDATE tier -- the first target from outside the deserialize tier. Ranked MINEABLE (0 removed public API) and then SHAPE-checked, which is the step that matters: mybatis 3.5.6 and avro 1.11.3 both passed the API check and were still dead ends, one because it RELAXES a restriction and one because its new restriction is OPT-IN. This boundary is neither -- the restriction is ACTIVE BY DEFAULT and the library ships a purpose-built method to opt back out of it, which is the strongest available evidence that real clients broke.
breaks.why_it_breaks: Before 3.9.0, FTPClient took the data-connection host from whatever the server put in its PASV reply, so a malicious server could redirect the data connection anywhere (CVE-2021-37533). 3.9.0 DISCARDS that host by default and uses the control connection's address instead: _parsePassiveModeReply now gates the old path behind isIpAddressFromPasvResponse(), whose backing field defaults to Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty(FTP_IP_ADDRESS_FROM_PASV_RESPONSE)) -- false when unset. The library's own comment labels the gated branch "Pre-3.9.0 behavior". BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-10 on JDK 11, no FTP server needed: feed the SAME reply '227 Entering Passive Mode (192,168,1,50,4,1)' to both jars via the protected _parsePassiveModeReply and read getPassiveHost(). 3.8.0 -> 192.168.1.50 (trusts the reply). 3.9.0 -> the reply host is discarded. 3.9.0 with setIpAddressFromPasvResponse(true) -> 192.168.1.50 again. A clean three-state differential: baseline, break, adaptation. setIpAddressFromPasvResponse does NOT EXIST in 3.8.0 -- it was added at the boundary FOR the clients this broke, which is both the adaptation to mine for and the reason to believe the population exists. Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit: the xstream allowTypes shape. Zero public API removed, so clients compile unchanged and fail at run time. Blast radius is narrower than xstream's -- it bites clients whose FTP server reports a different host in PASV, typically behind NAT -- so expect a small population rather than a dense one.

verify.note: Boundary pinned empirically (see why_it_breaks). Probe subclasses FTPClient, calls the protected _parsePassiveModeReply on a fixed PASV reply, and reads getPassiveHost() -- no server required.

breaks._provenance_note: Found 2026-08-10 by asking whether a BBC can hide UNDER a syntactic break. snakeyaml was already in the catalog as `snakeyaml-1.x-to-2.0-safeconstructor` and mined to a zero -- but every one of that entry's search terms targets the TAG/DESERIALIZATION break (TagInspector, SafeConstructor, 'Global tag is not allowed', CVE-2022-1471), whose adaptations are constructor-arity fixes forced by javac. The RESOURCE LIMITS are a separate behavioural break in the same library, at a different boundary, and were never searched for. Confirmed instance already in hand: Enterprise-Content-Management/infoarchive-sip-sdk@4b617cd8 raises codePointLimit in a commit whose PARENT already had `new SafeConstructor(new LoaderOptions())` -- the compile break was fixed earlier, and this commit is a PURE behavioural adaptation. Population probe: 41 client commits across setCodePointLimit (15), setMaxAliasesForCollections (16) and setAllowDuplicateKeys (10).
breaks.why_it_breaks:
1.32 imposes a 3 MB (3145728 code point) limit on incoming YAML BY DEFAULT and adds LoaderOptions.setCodePointLimit to raise it. BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-10 on JDK 11 with a PLAIN `new Yaml()` -- no configuration, i.e. what an unsuspecting client has:
  1.31  2 MB -> OK   4 MB -> OK    setCodePointLimit ABSENT
  1.32  2 MB -> OK   4 MB -> THROWS YAMLException 'The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.'
  1.32 + setCodePointLimit(10MB)  4 MB -> OK
A clean three-state differential. Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit, the xstream allowTypes shape, and UNLIKE the 1.x->2.0 boundary there is no constructor removal to shadow it: after normalising modifiers that cannot break a caller's source, 1.31->1.32 removes exactly ONE signature, setProcessComments(boolean), whose return type widened from void to LoaderOptions -- source-compatible for statement calls. So a client compiles unchanged and fails at run time. Blast radius: clients parsing YAML documents over 3 MB. Narrower than xstream, but the population is measured rather than assumed.

verify.note: Boundary pinned empirically (see why_it_breaks). Probe: plain `new Yaml()` loading a 4 MB scalar document returns on 1.31 and throws on 1.32.

breaks._provenance_note: Sibling of snakeyaml-1.31-to-1.32-codepointlimit in a DIFFERENT artifact. Found 2026-08-12 via a near-miss: fglock/PerlOnJava raises the code-point limit to 50 MB and looked like a case for the org.yaml:snakeyaml break, but it uses org.snakeyaml.engine.v2 -- the YAML 1.2 engine, a separate artifact with its own version line and an analogous limit. The adaptation identifier `setCodePointLimit` is spelled identically in both, so any search keyed on the identifier alone will mix them; find_adaptations.py confirms the library from the diff for exactly this reason.
breaks.why_it_breaks:
2.5 imposes the same 3 MiB (3145728 code point) ceiling snakeyaml 1.32 introduced, BY DEFAULT, and adds LoadSettingsBuilder.setCodePointLimit to raise it. BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-12 on JDK 11 with plain default settings -- `new Load(LoadSettings.builder().build()).loadFromString(doc)`:
  2.3  4 MB -> OK
  2.4  4 MB -> OK
  2.5  4 MB -> THROWS YamlEngineException 'The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.'
So the boundary is 2.4 -> 2.5, not 2.3 -> 2.4. Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit, the xstream allowTypes shape.

SCREEN CAVEAT, recorded rather than silently overridden: javap reports 7 removed public signatures across this boundary, so rank_candidates would REJECT it. All seven are raw generic types being parameterised (LoadSettings.getDefaultList: IntFunction<List> -> IntFunction<List<Object>>, and the matching setters, plus MappingNode.setValue). Those are source-compatible for ordinary lambda call sites though not for an explicitly-typed variable, and NONE is on the code-point-limit path, which is LoadSettings.builder().setCodePointLimit(n).build(). An eighth apparent removal, `public static final ... builder()` losing `final`, was a normalisation gap and is fixed.

verify.note: Boundary pinned empirically (see why_it_breaks). Probe: new Load(LoadSettings.builder().build()).loadFromString(4 MB doc) returns on 2.4 and throws on 2.5.

breaks.why_it_breaks:
1.26 caps the number of aliases for non-scalar nodes at 50 BY DEFAULT and adds LoaderOptions.setMaxAliasesForCollections to change it. BOUNDARY PINNED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-12 on JDK 11 with a plain `new Yaml()` -- no configuration, which is what an unsuspecting client has:
  1.25  40 aliases -> OK   60 aliases -> OK
  1.26  40 aliases -> OK   60 aliases -> THROWS YAMLException 'Number of aliases for non-scalar nodes exceeds the specified max=50'
Deny-by-default with an explicit re-permit, the same shape as the code-point limit.

SCREEN CAVEAT, recorded rather than overridden. javap reports 20 removed public signatures, and unlike the engine boundary these are REAL removals, not modifier or generics artifacts: ScalarAnalysis.allowBlock (a public field) and Event.is(Event$ID) across the event hierarchy. They are low-level emitter/parser internals that a client calling Yaml.load() never touches, so the behavioural change is reachable for ordinary clients -- but a client that DID use snakeyaml's event API would hit javac first and the behavioural break would be shadowed for them. Narrower risk than snakeyaml 2.0's constructor removal, not zero.

detail.corroborates: Independently re-derived on 2026-08-15 WITHOUT seeing _outcome_2026_08_12 on the same entry, which had already reached the same verdict on 2026-08-12 by the same route. Two assessments agree. The duplicated effort happened because assessments are recorded under TWO different key names (yield_status vs _outcome_<date>) and only yield_status was checked. Consolidate on yield_status. The earlier record additionally makes a point this one missed: a FIXED limit met by GROWING data is not a behavioural break, however genuine the resulting fix looks — distinct from born-past-boundary, and worth carrying as its own exclusion category.
detail._outcome_2026_08_12:
WORKED, NO CASES -- and the reason is the boundary's AGE, which is worth carrying to any future target. find_adaptations.py found 27 commits: 4 raises, 5 knobs at the default 50, 5 hardening, 7 needing a read. The raises are genuine, but the crossings evaporate:
  CatServer            born past  -- stayed at 1.27 across its whole history
  jdxia/shardingsphere crossed 1.16 -> 1.30 (2022-02), but that is a fork of apache and the alias fix is 2024, two years later
  Mirantis, kangarko   no declared version anywhere (Jenkins shared library / managed)
  liquibase            genuine raise to Integer.MAX_VALUE with a symptom-matching message ('YAML changelogs with many references', 2025-05-30), but NO crossing is locatable: liquibase-core/pom.xml shows snakeyaml 1.24 in 2019 then drops the declaration, and liquibase-standard/pom.xml only begins in 2023 at 2.0. The 1.25 -> 1.26 transition falls in a gap left by module restructuring.

1.26 shipped in 2020, three years before the code-point limit. By now essentially every client is on 2.x, and those that did cross did so long ago in build files that have since been reorganised. The code-point break yielded three cases because it was recent enough that crossings were still traceable; this one is not.

A SEPARATE POINT the liquibase commit makes well: their limit did not change, their DATA grew past it. A fixed limit met by growing input is not a behavioural breaking change, however genuine the resulting fix looks. Worth distinguishing from 'born past the boundary' -- the client may well have crossed, but the crossing changed nothing for them at the time.

_assessment: EVERY break carries exactly one `assessment` block. Read it BEFORE spending a mining run. This field exists because assessments were previously scattered across yield_status, _outcome_<date>, rejection_finding and verify_status, and checking only one of them caused the same break to be mined twice on 2026-08-15. status: yielded_cases | dead_screened_out | measured_zero | not_mined. `measured` is copied from output/reports/CENSUS.md (regenerated by ledger/census.py) — if the two disagree, the census wins. `unexploited_leads` is the ONLY field that means work remaining rather than a finding: candidates that reached traversal or production-adaptation status and were never taken further. `reason` and `detail` carry the prose from whichever key it was consolidated from, named in `consolidated_from`. measured_zero WITHOUT a reason means the numbers are known but nobody recorded WHY it yielded nothing — not the same as dead_screened_out, which carries a diagnosis.
